summary: Defines how IANA manages the object identifier tree under the Remote Monitoring (rmon) root, and records the values assigned so far. This is the registry procedure for RMON MIB modules.

eli5.summary: Network devices use numbered labels in a big tree. This tells the keeper of the numbers how to hand out new labels in the monitoring branch.

questions: how to get a number under rmon
subtitle: How IANA hands out numbers in the Remote Monitoring branch of the MIB tree, plus the list of numbers already used.

tldr.problem: The RMONMIB Working Group had kept its own list of object identifier assignments under the rmon root, which was a non-standard way to run a registry and had needed late corrections.
tldr.mechanism: IANA takes over the registry, lists the existing assignments, and from now on assigns only MODULE-IDENTITY (MIB root) numbers under the rmon node, through Standards Action.
tldr.outcome: New RMON MIB modules request a number in their document and IANA assigns it during RFC publication.

today: RFC 3737 is a Proposed Standard from April 2004, and the unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The text itself says IANA keeps the registry in its smi-numbers registry.

sections.title: Why the Registry Moves to IANA
sections.content:
The RMONMIB Working Group had so far kept its own registry of Object Identifier (OID) assignments under the rmon root of RFC 2819. It worked reasonably well, but errors had to be corrected at a late stage once or twice, and a few now defunct assignments had been made.

It was also unusual. Normally a new standards track MIB module gets its MIB root when it is published as an RFC. So this document lists the current assignments, sets out the rules for new ones, and asks IANA to take over responsibility for existing and future assignments.

The authors admit the current assignments are not very logical: normal MIB OIDs were first assigned under rmon, and later the working group used the rmon root to create new MIB modules beneath it. That history cannot be changed. From now on, only MODULE-IDENTITY macro (MIB root) assignments will be made by IANA under the rmon node.
sections.eli5: One group kept its own list of numbers, which was a bit messy. Now the official number-keeper takes over the list.

sections.title: Numbers Already Assigned
sections.content:
The assignments under mib-2.rmon (1.3.6.1.2.1.16) were maintained by the RMONMIB Working Group until this RFC was published. IANA has picked them up in its existing smi-numbers registry.

The first table lists numbers { rmon nnn } from 0 to 32. Entries 0 to 9 come from RFC 2819 (statistics, history, alarm, hosts, hostTopN, matrix, filter, capture, event, plus the notifications root at 0). Entry 10 is tokenRing from RFC 1513, and entries 11 to 20 come from RFC 2021. Later entries are module roots such as switchRMON (22, RFC 2613), apm (23, RFC 3729), dsmonMIB (26, RFC 3287), interfaceTopNMIB (27, RFC 3144) and hcAlarmMIB (29, RFC 3434).

Some entries are special. Number 24 is available, number 25 (pmCapsMIB) is defunct, and numbers 28, 30, 31 and 32 are reserved for sspmMIB, tpmMIB, raqmon and raqmonDs, which were still Internet-Drafts.

A second table covers the rmonConformance node (1.3.6.1.2.1.16.20), with ten entries for compliance and group definitions and for hcRMON (5) and rmonMibModule (8).
sections.eli5: The RFC prints the full list of drawer numbers already used, and marks which ones are free, reserved or no longer in use.

sections.title: How to Request a New Assignment
sections.content:
An author of an Internet-Draft who needs a number under the rmon OID writes the MIB module with a placeholder. The module imports rmon from RMON-MIB, defines a MODULE-IDENTITY, and ends with ::= { rmon nnn } followed by a note asking IANA to assign nnn and asking the RFC Editor to replace it and remove the note.

IANA assigns the number as part of the RFC publication process. Within the new module, the authors and editors then assign their own OIDs by the normal procedures.
sections.eli5: When you write a new monitoring document, you leave a blank where the number goes. The number-keeper fills it in when the document is published.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA has integrated the initial set of assignments into the existing smi-numbers registry and is requested to maintain the registry for future assignments. New assignments can only be made via Standards Action, as described in RFC 2434, the guidelines for writing an IANA Considerations section.
sections.eli5: New numbers are only given out for documents that have gone through the full standards process.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC describes procedures for IANA assignment of OBJECT IDENTIFIER values and states that it has no impact on the security of the Internet. It adds no protocol and changes no behavior of any monitored device.
sections.eli5: It is just a numbering rule, so it does not change how safe anything is.

data.title: Requesting a number under rmon
data.code:
EXAMPLE-MIB DEFINITIONS ::= BEGIN

IMPORTS
  rmon          FROM RMON-MIB

  .. other imports ..

exampleMIB  MODULE-IDENTITY

  ... other normal MODULE-IDENTITY stuff ...

::= { rmon nnn }  -- IANA: please assign nnn
                  -- RFC-Editor: replace nnn with IANA-assigned
                  --             number and remove this note
